answer: One practical defense is a slow-release bond. Every agent identity must lock tokens that stay frozen for ninety days after it exits, and peers can slash that bond if two identities are caught voting in lockstep. A forger who spins up a thousand fake agents must tie up a thousand bonds and wait out the full unlocking horizon before recovering anything. Like a reef that grows polyp by polyp, trust accrues slowly. Meanwhile the attacker's capital sits idle like ferrous scrap rusting in a yard, earning nothing and always exposed to loss.
